summary: Origin planes, axes and the origin point are selectable in the 3D view, and a selected plane can cut a section view. The model view shows the reference geometry: the XY, XZ and YZ planes as translucent patches sized to the part with a margin and a smallest size, the X, Y and Z axes across the part, the origin point as a marker a few pixels across, and every active datum plane. The planes and axes change size in steps, so they are rebuilt only when the part outgrows a step, not on every build. Show reference geometry in the View drawer hides them, leaving the selected plane or axis, the planes a command asks for and a plane whose tree row is hovered. Clicking a plane, an axis or the origin point selects it, with hover highlight and a pixel tolerance on axes and the point. Material in front wins: the part is picked where it is in front of a plane, an axis or the origin point, a datum plane where it is in front of the part, the origin point and axes before an origin plane they lie in, and an origin plane only where nothing else is under the pointer. One function maps a selection to the input a command takes: a selected plane starts Sketch, Curve and Plane on it, gives Mirror its mirror plane and enables Section view; a selected axis gives Circular pattern its axis through the origin, and Revolve its axis when it is the same line as one of the sketch's own axes, compared by direction and by distance between the lines at the native placement precision; a selection a command cannot use stops the command with its reason instead of falling back to a default. Section view, in the View drawer and in a datum plane's menus, clips every body, sketch and curve outline by the plane with one shared clipping plane, removing the side the plane normal points to; Flip keeps the other side. Caps, on by default, fill the cut material with a flat colour. They are drawn on the plane from each body's triangles, built once for each plane and each mesh upload, and fill wherever the cut winds round a point, so they show wherever the camera stands, inside the kept material or with the near plane through it. Solids of one body that lie inside or overlap each other are filled as one, holes through the cut and cavities stay open, and a body whose triangles do not close gets no cap. They are never picked, listed or exported. Picking and hover skip the removed side: the ray is limited to the kept side, and edges and sketch or curve outlines within a pick's pixel tolerance are measured only to the part the section keeps. The section is kept on the device for the document it was made in, as a versioned record; it survives rebuilds, follows its datum plane when that moves, turns off when the datum plane is deleted or suppressed, gives way to an open sketch's or curve's own view and returns when it closes. Escape in the model view clears a selection first and then turns the section off. Filter in the View drawer chooses what hover and clicks can select: bodies, faces, edges, planes, axes and the origin point; commands that ask for a pick keep their own rules. Agents turn the section on by the selected plane, change its side and caps, and turn it off with the set-section viewport command, which runs the same operation as the control.
warning: No breaking change for CAD files, installed posts, machine packages, saved revisions or controller output. Potentially breaking for automation and for users who relied on the old picture or clicks. The model view now shows the origin axes and point and every active datum plane by default, and the origin plane patches are sized to the part instead of a fixed 25 mm square, so screenshots change and a click on empty space inside the part's extent can now select an origin plane where it used to clear the selection; turn Show reference geometry off, or exclude Planes in Filter, for the earlier behaviour. With a datum plane selected, Mirror now stops with a reason instead of starting about its default plane; with an origin axis selected that is not the same line as one of the sketch's own axes (within 1e-7 mm, and an angle within the frames' rounding), Revolve now stops with a reason instead of starting about the sketch's default axis. The View drawer in the model view gains Section view, Flip section, Caps, Show reference geometry, Filter and a help button, so automation that counts its controls or tab stops must allow for them, and a datum plane's menus gain Section view. Escape in the model view with nothing selected now turns an active section off. The model view's renderer now asks for a stencil buffer, which section caps count in. cad_set_viewport gains the set-section command, and the descriptions of cad_get_viewport and cad_set_viewport are shorter, without a change in behaviour, to keep tool discovery under its budget. cad_get_viewport gains section (null or {plane, flip, caps}), selectedOrigin while an origin axis or the origin point is selected, and view.section while a section is drawn. Device preferences under wire-edm:cad-preferences:v1 gain an optional versioned section record, showReferenceGeometry and selectionFilter; release 0.0.788 and earlier ignore them and drop them the next time they write the preferences, which turns the section off and shows reference geometry with every kind selectable.

checklist.schema: No CAD document, sketch, UPID, post, machine package, saved revision, storage, journal or worker protocol change, and no new document reference type. Device preferences (localStorage wire-edm:cad-preferences:v1) gain three optional fields: section {version: 1, documentId, plane: 'XY' | 'XZ' | 'YZ' | {kind: 'datum-plane', featureId}, flip, caps}, written while a section is on and read only for the same document and version; showReferenceGeometry, written only as false; and selectionFilter {excluded: [...]} of body, face, edge, vertex, plane, axis and point, written only when something is excluded, with unknown kinds dropped on reading so they stay selectable. A value this release cannot read is ignored and the other preferences stay in force; stored bytes are never rewritten except by an explicit choice. The part view (section, reference geometry and filter) sits beside the sketch view in src/features/cad/view/cadViewState.ts, and its section plane type stays open for later references. Post engine API remains 1 and saved-job engine remains 3.
checklist.events: No execution event or input-version behavior change. Hover reads the installed meshes and reference geometry only: no kernel or worker request, no rebuild, and at most one frame request per hover change. Reference geometry is rebuilt only when the build or the part's size step changes; the section's clipping plane is one shared object updated in place. Caps are built on the main thread once for each plane and each mesh upload while a capped section shows, never on a frame or a hover. A body whose box the plane misses is skipped before its triangles are prepared. Other builds run in slices of about 6 ms, each ending after the step that passes it, so input keeps its turn; caps that finish in a later slice draw one more frame. A build that a new plane, mesh upload or hiding replaces is dropped and none of its caps is shown. A 5,292-triangle plate with 40 holes prepares in 1.2 to 9.3 ms and caps in 0.1 to 1.5 ms; a 480,000-triangle body prepares in 66.8 to 90.7 ms and caps in 3.8 to 8.2 ms, spread over slices of at most 8.1 to 9.1 ms. Each cut body draws three times: two passes count in the stencil buffer how the cut winds round each pixel, and one quad fills where the count is not zero and clears it. Line picks with no section, and reference geometry a section does not cut, take three.js's hits as they are and check only the world tolerance again. The pick filter limits the ray's near and far distances to the kept side, and lines a section cuts are measured to their kept part. Translucent plane patches draw in one pass instead of three.js's back-then-front passes, which looked up each patch's shader program twice a frame; a flat patch shows the same pixels either way. The section turns off before paint when its datum plane is deleted or suppressed, and an open sketch or curve replaces it without clearing the stored choice. Agent set-section runs through the same guarded operation as the control: WRONG_VIEW during sketch or curve editing, VIEW_UNAVAILABLE before the model view renders, INVALID_INPUT without a selected plane when turning on, and NOT_FOUND for a datum plane that is missing or suppressed.
checklist.capabilities: No post or machine capability change. WebMCP: cad_set_viewport adds set-section {on, flip?, caps?}, which cuts by the plane that select-reference-plane or a feature selection chose; cad_get_viewport reports section, selectedOrigin and view.section. Tool discovery stays under its 50 KiB budget (51191 of 51200 bytes) by shortening the two viewport tool descriptions rather than raising the budget, which leaves little room for the next tool change. The View drawer in the model view adds Section view, Flip section, Caps, Show reference geometry and Filter, with help; a datum plane's menus add Section view. Not included: showing or hiding single planes from the tree, a Select other cycle through overlapping candidates, vertex picks in 3D (the filter keeps that kind for later), mirroring about a datum plane, revolving about an axis that is not one of the sketch's own, sizing datum plane patches to the part, and a document reference type for origin axes and the point. The shared UI components and theme are unchanged.
checklist.auditAndOutput: No generation, audit, numbering, encoding, line ending, feed or controller-file change. Caps and the section are view-only and never reach STEP, STL, DXF, CAM sections or saved files; viewport captures show what the view shows.
checklist.installationAndStorage: No installed package, revision, browser-cache or folder storage change. The section, reference geometry and filter choices live only in the device preference key above, in browser local storage, and are not saved in documents, the browser cache workbench or the folder adapter.
checklist.verification: New unit suites: cadReferenceSelection (the one selection-to-command mapping: planes for Sketch, Curve, Section view and Plane, origin planes for Mirror, origin axes for Circular pattern and for Revolve only when the same line as one of the sketch's own axes, refusing a sketch axis turned 0.002° about Z and one at [6000000, 0.005, 0] or offset 1e-6 mm, accepting the same far line exactly and quarter or rolled turns that keep the axis, lines compared by direction either way round and by distance counting the angle over the distance between them, the reason thrown instead of a default, other drafts untouched), cadSectionView (clip through the plane origin with a tolerance for faces on it, the clip sense of both sides, the ray limited to the kept side from either side of the plane and parallel to it, boxes removed whole, a datum section that follows edits and lets the view turn off when suppressed or deleted, frames compared by value, line hits never landing on a removed segment however close to the cut and measured to a crossing segment's kept part, indexed or not, and with no plane taken from three.js along the whole ray as a plane keeping everything would measure them, the world tolerance checked again, applied to edge and outline picks while uncut references stay pickable), cadSectionCaps (the covered area and winding of caps of a closed body whose faces repeat their shared points, on the plane, from either side and none when the plane misses; holes open and an island inside a hole filled; solids one inside another and overlapping solids filled wholly; a cut through vertex rows; a face lying on the plane left to draw itself; open shells and a body with a face turned inside out given no cap; several bodies capped where they lie, one at [6000000, 0.005, 0.5] in its own coordinates, none for a body missed or open; caps rebuilt once for each plane and upload and kept while hidden; a body the plane misses skipped without reading its triangles; a large body built in slices, with a stale continuation, a new upload and hiding each dropping the build and none of its caps shown), cadSectionCapsImport (STEP files imported and built in the kernel as File > Import does: a box inside a box fills 100 mm² where nesting gave 84, overlapping boxes fill their 175 mm² union where nesting gave 100, a hollow solid keeps its 4 mm cavity open at 84 mm², and boxes that touch along a face, whose shared edges four triangles use, fill 200 mm² where the second draft gave no cap), cadPartView (the section reducer, refused planes, sketch precedence and return, the versioned per-document record and reading back only a complete one, the selection filter and its stored form with unknown kinds dropped, reference geometry), CadViewportSection (bodies and outlines clipped while reference geometry stays whole, flip, a rebuild keeping the section, caps on each closed body the section cuts as geometry on the clip plane, only while on, reused while the plane stays and rebuilt when it moves, never pickable or listed, an outline the section removes never picked from beside the cut and a kept one picked from past it, picks through the cut, origin axis and point picks and their filters, a body in front winning over a plane and the plane winning once bodies are filtered out), CadPlaneSelectionSection (the reference geometry list and toggle, the filter menu stored and restored, Plane and Revolve from a selected reference and the Revolve reason, Section view on, flip, caps, its stored record per document and the staged Escape, a datum section that follows edits, gives way to a sketch, turns off on suppress and delete and stays off, agent set-section with its errors, the tree menu entry). Existing suites pass unchanged except CadSketchPlaneFlow, whose datum hover test now turns reference geometry off, because datum planes are shown with it, and which gains a test that every active datum plane shows with the reference geometry. Mutations, each caught and then reverted: an unlimited pick ray (3 unit tests and the Chromium pick-through check fail), the clip sense inverted (9 unit tests and the Chromium section normal fail), caps drawn while off (1 unit test and the Chromium cap colour fail), the selection filter accepting everything (4 unit tests fail), the distance between lines ignored (3 unit tests fail), the angle over that distance ignored (1 unit test fails), a scale-relative line tolerance (2 unit tests fail), the clip ignored in line hits (2 unit tests, the viewport outline test and the Chromium edge test fail), outlines left uncut (the viewport outline test fails), -0 not joined with 0 (the vertex row, skip and slicing tests fail), the first draft's stencil caps of body surfaces (the Chromium camera-inside test fails, the cut reading as background), the second draft's caps that filled loops by nesting (the nested, overlapping and touching import tests fail), an even-odd count instead of the winding (the Chromium imported-solids test fails, the inner box and the overlap reading grey), the closedness check skipped (the open shell and several-bodies tests fail), the bounds skip removed (the skip test fails), stale slices not dropped (the slicing test fails), and the world tolerance not checked again with no plane (the no-plane line hit test fails). Chromium spec e2e/cad-plane-selection-section.spec.ts, 5 tests: picks each origin plane, axis and the origin point in the Top, Front and Right views at projected positions, checks the canvas is what is under the pointer, starts a sketch on a picked XZ; cuts by it, reads the cap colour on the cut bar against the uncapped and uncut views, reads which side is removed in Top against an empty baseline, flips it, picks through the cut, opens and closes a sketch, checks the stored record and turns it off with Escape; picks an edge 2 px past the cut and within its tolerance only when no section removes it; caps a 60 mm round tunnel with a 4 mm bore, the bore left open, while the camera stands inside the kept tunnel and while the tunnel ends 0.005 mm before the camera inside its near distance, and shows the cut open with caps off; exports six bodies as one STEP file, imports it as one body of six solids and reads the cap on a box inside a box, on overlapping boxes and on Bar's wall, with Bar's enclosed pocket open. Single specs on the final production build, each alone with 2 workers: cad-plane-selection-section (5), cad-sketch-view-modes (4), cad-workflow (32), cad-topology-repick (3), all passed. Full Vitest: 580 files, 6797 tests passed. npm run build, lint (zero findings), ui:check, the e2e type check and check-release passed, check-release also against origin/main at 0.0.788. Cap build, timed in Vitest: a 5,292-triangle plate with 40 holes prepares in 1.2 to 9.3 ms and caps in 0.1 to 1.5 ms; a 480,000-triangle box prepares in 66.8 to 90.7 ms and caps in 3.8 to 8.2 ms, once per upload and plane. Turning a capped section on with a 480,000-triangle body the plane misses took 60.0 to 87.5 ms in one task before round 2, and now 2.7 to 3.6 ms on the first plane after an upload, for the body's box, and 0.01 to 0.04 ms after; with that body crossed, one task of 61.8 to 79.2 ms became 11 to 15 slices of at most 8.1 to 9.1 ms, 68.5 to 97.1 ms in all. Hover at 4x CPU in Chromium with SwiftShader, three rotated rounds of four modes on a 40-hole plate, on the final build: P50 56.8 ms with reference geometry, 41.4 ms without, 46.1 ms with a section and 49.7 ms with caps, in a session about 5 ms slower throughout than the one before; caps measured 7.3, 2.4 and 7.5 ms slower than the section alone in the same rounds, where the second draft's caps had measured 2.3 ms faster to 3.2 ms slower and the first draft's 10.1 to 14.5 ms slower. Reference geometry shown measured 13.2, 13.5 and 15.4 ms slower than hidden in those rounds and 3.8, 9.0 and 1.6 ms in three more rounds of the two alone, against 5.5 to 14.5 ms before the no-plane line hit path, which saves about 1 µs of a 91 µs pick in Vitest; no worker message and 150 or 151 frames for 149 or 150 moves in every run (docs/maintainers/cad-performance.md). No controller or machine verification is claimed.

publicNotes.summary: Origin planes, axes and the origin point can be picked in the 3D view, and a picked plane can cut a section view.
changes: The 3D view shows the XY, XZ and YZ planes sized to your part, the X, Y and Z axes, the origin point and your datum planes. Show reference geometry in View hides them.

Click a plane, an axis or the origin point to select it. A selected plane starts Sketch, Curve and Plane on it and gives Mirror its plane; a selected axis gives Circular pattern and Revolve their axis.

Section view in View, or in a datum plane's menu, cuts the view by the selected plane. Flip keeps the other side, Caps fills the cut material, and Escape turns the section off once nothing is selected. Clicks reach only what the section keeps.
Filter in View chooses what you can point at and click: bodies, faces, edges, planes, axes and the origin point.
These choices are remembered in this browser, and the section only for the part you made it in.
publicNotes.compatibility: No file or schema change. Installed machine packages, posts, saved revisions and controller output are unchanged. Agents gain the set-section viewport command.
publicNotes.action: No action is needed. Turn Show reference geometry off, or exclude Planes in Filter, if you prefer clicks on empty space to clear the selection as before.
